page.content:
Dictator who crossed the Rubicon and died on the Ides of March.

How Julius Caesar connects

  • Event: Assassination of Caesar — The Ides of March killed Caesar.
  • Work: Commentarii de Bello Gallico — Caesar wrote the Gallic War commentaries.
  • Event: Crossing the Rubicon — Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon opened the civil war.
  • Character: Pompey — Caesar and Pompey fought the civil war that ended at Pharsalus.
  • Character: Augustus — Augustus was Caesar's adopted heir and avenger.
  • Character: Mark Antony — Antony was Caesar's lieutenant and avenger.
  • Faction: Roman legion — Caesar's loyalty-bound legions made the Rubicon possible.
  • Character: Cicero — Cicero defended Republican forms against Caesar's dictatorship and Antony's aftermath.

What is Julius Caesar?

Gaius Julius Caesar conquered Gaul, broke Pompey, and made himself dictator perpetuo. His murder in 44 BCE did not restore the Republic; it opened the last civil wars.

Key threads lead to Assassination of Caesar, Commentarii de Bello Gallico, Crossing the Rubicon, Pompey, Augustus and Mark Antony.
